title: Ginza, der Schatz der Mandaer (German)
author: Mark Lidzbarski (trans)
description: Ginza: Der Schatz oder das grosse Buch der Mandäer (The Treasure, or the Great Book of the Mandaeans), translated into German and annotated by Mark Lidzbarski (Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht; Leipzig: J. C. Hinrichs, 1925). The Ginza Rba is the principal holy book of the Mandaeans, the Gnostic baptist community of Iraq and Iran. It is divided into the Right Ginza, containing cosmology, theology, myths of creation and of the world of light and darkness, the descent of the saviour Manda d-Hayye, moral teachings, and polemics against Judaism, Christianity and Islam; and the Left Ginza, consisting of hymns and texts on the ascent of the soul after death through the watch-houses to the world of light. Lidzbarski's translation, based on the Petermann edition, with introductions and notes, remains the standard scholarly translation and the basis of most later study of Mandaean religion.
